origins.section: Precedence and Associativity Group an Expression; Its Operands Still Run Left to Right
Precedence and Associativity Group an Expression; Its Operands Still Run Left to Right
Integer Division Truncates Toward Zero, and % Takes the Sign of the Dividend
Bit Operators Bind Looser Than ==, and an int Shift Counts Only to 31

gates.says: all 4 of this quiz's answerable readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-index-then-increment: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-index-then-increment: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-index-then-increment: Option a is right, and the page supports both halves of it. The index part comes from L91-92: "Assignment works the same way: in `a[i] = ...`, the index is read before the right side runs." So slots[0] is the target. The value part comes from L79: "`retries++` has a value, the old one", so i++ gives 0 and the sum is 10. The `says` is correct. One flag: the stem asks what both `slots` and `i` hold, but no option gives i's final value (1). [Applied: stem now asks which element is set and to what.]
recorded.prompt:q-log-concatenation: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-log-concatenation: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-log-concatenation: Option b is fully supported by L84-86: "Operators of equal precedence group left to right, and `+` with a `String` on either side concatenates. `"Total: " + 10` is already a string, so `+ 20` appends "20"." The summary also says "`"s" + 1 + 2` concatenates".
recorded.prompt:q-weekday-remainder: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-weekday-remainder: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-weekday-remainder: Option a is fully supported by L50-52: "Java defines it so that `(a / b) * b + a % b == a`, which gives the remainder the dividend's sign. `-3 % 60` is `-3`, and as an index into a 60-slot array it throws `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException`." -8 % 7 = -1.
recorded.prompt:q-shift-into-long: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-shift-into-long: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-shift-into-long: Option c is fully supported by L180-182: "an `int` shift uses only the low five bits of its distance: 35 becomes 3, and the result, 8, is widened to `long` afterwards." 33 becomes 1, 1 << 1 = 2. Edge table `1 << 32` gives `1`.

recorded.prompt:q-index-then-increment:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-index-then-increment:b: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-index-then-increment:b: Refuted by L90-92: "Java evaluates the left operand of every binary operator fully before the right one ... in `a[i] = ...`, the index is read before the right side runs." Partly true: the claim that i++ yields 0 is correct (L79). Only the claim about order is wrong.

recorded.outcome:q-index-then-increment:c: Refuted by L79: "`retries++` has a value, the old one". So i++ yields 0, not 1. Partly true: the index part (slots[0]) is correct.

recorded.outcome:q-index-then-increment:d: Both claims are refuted: the order by L91-92 and the value by L79.
